questionsToConsider: Will the employee see their manager's assessment too, or is this only their side?
Do the competency rows match the ones in your job descriptions or review framework?
How long before the meeting should it be sent, so the manager has time to read it?
Should goals be pasted into the form, or will people have their last review to hand?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read each self-appraisal before the meeting and note where the employee's view and yours differ, especially on the competency grid and the overall rating: those gaps are the conversation. Treat the blockers answer as a list of things the organisation may need to fix, not excuses. Turn the support and next goals answers into written actions at the end of the meeting, and bring them back at the next review.
customizeSteps: Replace the competency rows with the ones your organisation reviews against.
Add a question for the manager's name if one link goes to the whole company, so each appraisal reaches the right reviewer.
Send it about a week before the review meeting, and agree with managers to read it before they write their own notes.

faqs.q: What should a performance appraisal survey include?
faqs.a: The goals agreed for the period, what got in the way, specific examples of good work, a self-rating, the support needed and goals for next time. That gives the review meeting a clear agenda.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a self-appraisal and a performance review?
faqs.a: A self-appraisal is the employee's own account, written before the meeting. The review is the conversation where it's compared with the manager's view and next steps are agreed.

faqs.q: How do I write good self-appraisal answers?
faqs.a: Be specific: name the piece of work, what you did and what changed because of it. Be honest about what didn't go well and what would help next time.
Yes. The form includes an optional upload for up to three files, such as reports or thank-you messages, which appear with the response in the dashboard.

doc.title: Performance appraisal
doc.description: Help employees prepare for their review with goals, examples, a self-rating and next steps.

blocks.title: Your review is coming up. This helps you and your manager start from the same page, and takes about ten minutes to answer thoughtfully.
Which period does this review cover?
Looking at the goals you agreed for this period, how many did you meet?
What got in the way of the goals you didn't reach?
blocks.description: Changed priorities, missing resources, things outside your control: all worth naming.

blocks.title: Describe two or three pieces of work you're proudest of this period.
blocks.description: Specific examples help most: what you did, and what changed because of it.

blocks.title: Want to attach anything that shows your work?
blocks.description: Optional. A report, a message of thanks, a screenshot.

blocks.title: How would you rate yourself on each of these?
Overall, how would you rate your performance this period?
What support from your manager or the company would help you most next period?
Which areas would you like to develop?
What goals would you like to set for the next period?
Anything else you want to make sure comes up in the meeting?
